clue.text: He went with his ass to a lake ere noon

definitions.text: He went with his ass to a lake ere noon

parts.words: He went with his ass to a lake ere noon
parts.note: an allusion to the Old Testament prophet who set out one morning riding his donkey, the beast that famously talked back to him

explanation.surface: A man takes his donkey down to a lake one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Numbers tells of the seer who saddled his ass and rode off to the king of Moab; 'a lake ere noon' plays on A, L (lake) and AM (morning) in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophet whose talking donkey rebuked him is the man who went off riding his ass.

clue.text: Displayed heraldically black boy holding belt

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: holding means the boy's word contains the belt's word

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a zone is a belt or girdle

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned lad wearing a belt shown as on a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To blazon is to describe or depict a coat of arms, so shown heraldically.

clue.text: Deuce of a match!

definitions.meaning: the deuce is an old euphemism for the devil
an old type of friction match

explanation.surface: Exclaiming what a devilish game that was!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deuce' looks like tennis, a match score; it is the devil, and 'match' is a striking match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is a name for Satan and was also a brand name for early friction matches.

clue.text: A race in which one leads men to expiation

indicators.note: in which means the following pieces sit inside the race

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: leads means one comes in front of men

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A competition in which a single leader heads the field to make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous Isle of Man motorcycle race; 'leads' means one comes first, ahead of men.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for wrongdoing, which is what expiation means.

clue.text: Signified by originators of occult knowledge

definitions.text: Signified by originators of occult knowledge

parts.words: Signified by originators of occult knowledge
parts.note: the first letters of 'occult knowledge' are O and K, and OK is what a nod of assent says

explanation.surface: Something hinted at by the founders of an esoteric tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occult' suggests mystic lore, but only its initial matters: the originators of 'occult knowledge' spell OK, the everyday sign of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying OK expresses assent, so OK is the sign of endorsement.

clue.text: I direct man."Pull out your air-power weapon"

indicators.note: out signals the letters being turned out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone instructs a man to draw his air gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I DIRECT MAN PULL; 'weapon' is facetious for a roadworker's compressed-air tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A compressed-air hammer drill used to break up roads is jocularly an air-powered weapon.

clue.text: Cynara's lover enjoyed his fling with them

definitions.text: Cynara's lover enjoyed his fling with them

parts.words: Cynara's lover enjoyed his fling with them
parts.note: Dowson's poem to Cynara: 'I flung ..., ... riotously with the throng', so the fling is literal throwing

explanation.surface: A man's affair with some unnamed others while loving Cynara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests an affair, but in Ernest Dowson's poem the lover throws flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the flowers the poem's speaker flung riotously.

clue.text: Doodlebug, love, coming over fast and furious.

parts.note: the doodlebug was the German V1 flying bomb of World War II
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A flying bomb comes overhead fast and fierce, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: V1, the wartime doodlebug, is written VI; 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun, Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging and wild behaviour is furious, or violent.

clue.text: Pussy enjoying lap of cream, and of this

definitions.text: Pussy enjoying lap of cream, and of this

parts.words: Pussy enjoying lap of cream, and of this
parts.note: a cat lapping cream is in the proverbial 'lap of' comfort and indulgence

explanation.surface: A cat happily laps up some cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lap' is both the cat's drinking and the idiom 'in the lap of' indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Great comfort and indulgence, as when one lives in the lap of it.

clue.text: Love of a laughing tippler -

parts.note: the old drinking song 'Ha ha ha, you and me, ... don't I love thee', addressed to a jug of liquor

explanation.surface: Who or what a cheerful drunk adores.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19th-century drinking song has the chorus 'Ha, ha, ha, you and me', hence 'laughing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The small earthenware jug of drink is what the song's tippler loves.

clue.text: Can their love transform this, lonely man?

indicators.note: to transform is to change shape, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question whether romance could change someone, with a solitary man overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transform' rearranges CAN, THEIR and O (love, nil in tennis scoring) into a recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit who withdraws from the world for religious reasons is a solitary man.

clue.text: Take this Indian to court? Sound idea for some

indicators.note: some people's idea of how the tribe's name is said, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: to sue is to court or woo, as in suing for a lady's hand, and also to take to law

explanation.surface: Should one prosecute this Native American? A sensible thought to some.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface joke is that to take someone to court is to sue them, and the tribe's name is pronounced just like that verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Constable in his spare time-is so eccentric

definitions.meaning: an off-duty police officer is away from his patrol round
unconventional or out of the ordinary

explanation.surface: A policeman, when off duty, is a bit of an oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: A constable's patrol is his beat, so off duty he is off his beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional behaviour departs from the normal rhythm, so it is quirky.

clue.text: Somebody's rubber?

parts.note: read 'Somebody' as 'some body': the person who rubs a body, a massage practitioner

explanation.surface: Whose eraser is this?
explanation.definitionFit: A massage practitioner rubs other people's bodies for a living.

clue.text: Circuit round one mountain' stronghold

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: an eyre was a circuit court of itinerant judges in medieval England
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A loop encircles a single mountain fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyre is the old English name for the circuit of travelling justices; 'round' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a crag is a lofty, secure refuge, a mountain stronghold.

clue.text: In which certain players' interrupt others

definitions.text: In which certain players' interrupt others

parts.words: In which certain players' interrupt others
parts.note: the orchestra's musicians break into the actors' performance by playing between the acts

explanation.surface: Describes some performers butting in on other performers.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval piece of music played between acts of a stage show puts the musicians in place of the actors.

clue.text: First model for a flood-survivor, might one say?

indicators.note: might one say asks us to hear the words spoken, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: Noah's ark survived the Flood, so a model of the right type for it is an ark type

explanation.surface: Asks about an original prototype for someone who came through a deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'ark-type' sounds like the word for an original pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern from which copies are made, a first model.

clue.text: Saturnian technology Stephenson anticipated

parts.note: the Saturn V moon launcher and George Stephenson's locomotive the Rocket share a name

explanation.surface: Engineering about Saturn that a railway pioneer foresaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephenson's Rocket was the famous 1829 steam locomotive; Saturn rockets launched the Apollo missions.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of propulsion by rockets is the technology of Saturn launchers.

clue.text: Gladstone, sophistical exponent of this (Disraeli)

parts.note: Disraeli called Gladstone 'a sophistical ..., inebriated with the exuberance of his own verbosity'

explanation.surface: Disraeli's jibe at his rival Gladstone as a slippery speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Gladstone and Disraeli were rival Victorian prime ministers; the clue quotes Disraeli's famous insult.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of persuasive speech is what a sophistical orator practises.

clue.text: What's your poison, Partlet?

parts.note: Partlet is the hen in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale; the bane of a hen is a poisonous plant

explanation.surface: A barman asks someone called Partlet what they will drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's your poison' is a drinks offer; Pertelote or Partlet is the traditional name for a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous nightshade plant whose name says it is harmful to fowl.

clue.text: Contents of many an ancient, vessel

definitions.text: Contents of many an ancient, vessel

parts.words: Contents of many an ancient, vessel
parts.note: what a ship carries in its hold, as in Masefield's poem about the quinquireme of Nineveh

explanation.surface: What old ships, or old pots, carried inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' could be a pot, but it is a ship; Masefield's 'Cargoes' lists the loads of ancient ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried in a ship's hold are its freight.

clue.text: Inexperienced blighters it could be said — harsh?

indicators.note: it could be said tells us to hear the phrase spoken

parts.note: raw means inexperienced and cuss is a blighter, a wretched fellow

explanation.surface: Asking whether calling novices rotters would be unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'raw cuss' sounds like the word for a loud, grating voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A raucous sound is rough and grating, harsh to the ear.

clue.text: A small catch for Hogarth's girl

definitions.meaning: a tiny crustacean caught in nets
Hogarth painted 'The ... Girl', a fishmonger's lass

explanation.surface: A tiny find for an artist's female model.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth, the 18th-century English painter, made the famous sketch 'The Shrimp Girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sea crustacean is a little catch and names Hogarth's girl.

clue.text: Woodcutter a rapacious bird? Mad to think so

definitions.meaning: a carpenter's saw for cutting timber by hand

definitions.text: a rapacious bird? Mad to think so
definitions.meaning: Hamlet, feigning madness, says he knows a hawk from this tool, perhaps a corruption of heronshaw

explanation.surface: Is a forester really a bird of prey? Only a madman would think so.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet: 'I am but mad north-north-west: when the wind is southerly I know a hawk from a handsaw.'
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-operated saw cuts wood; Hamlet's mad line pairs the tool with a hawk.

clue.text: Day's work for a bird

definitions.meaning: an allotted period or share of work
a small wading bird related to the sandpiper

explanation.surface: A day of labour for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotted spell of labour, and also a small sandpiper-like shore bird.

clue.text: Eggs a dollar? Sounds a little, dear

parts.note: roe is a mass of fish eggs
buck is slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: Someone haggling over the price of eggs, addressing a dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' tells you to hear 'dear' as 'deer': the answer is a small species of deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe species is one of the smallest European deer, so a male one is a little deer.

clue.text: Today's national sense of "Urgent Dichotomy"?

parts.note: read 'Ur-gent' as a gentleman of Ur, and the dichotomy as the land between two rivers, Mesopotamia, the modern Middle Eastern state

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what a pressing division means nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia, 'the land between the rivers' Tigris and Euphrates, now in Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern citizen of the country containing ancient Ur and Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Wherein crew of "a happy ship" have a row?

definitions.text: Wherein crew of "a happy ship" have a row?

parts.note: jolly means cheerful or happy
a boat is a vessel, a ship

explanation.surface: Even on a contented ship the crew can fall out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have a row' means a quarrel, but here it is rowing: a ship's small rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's small boat used for rowing to shore is where the crew pull oars.

clue.text: Reputation of tigers perhaps in Open — unlimited!

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the other piece
without limits, the word Open loses its first and last letters
perhaps suggests the letters of tigers may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: How golf's big championship rates players like Tiger Woods, without restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's oldest championship, and 'tigers' nods to Tiger Woods, but both are just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is standing or renown, a good reputation.

clue.text: A river, in my Gaelic tongue

indicators.note: in means the language goes inside the word my

parts.note: Erse is the Irish or Scottish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Naming a river in one's own Gaelic language.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mersey is the river of Liverpool in northwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mersey is a river in northwest England.
